os-blazor-settings.title: Settings admin page
os-blazor-settings.summary: A ready-made Blazor page where an administrator reads and edits the settings of OS.Settings: sections, scopes, validation, secrets, resets and conflict handling, with no form code of your own.

gives.1: One component, `OSSettingBoard`, that lists every settings section and opens each one for viewing or editing.
gives.2: Editing that is safe: values are checked in the browser with the same rules as the server, a change made on a stale version is flagged as a conflict, and secrets are never shown back.
gives.3: Per-scope values (for example per shop) that follow the whole-app value until you give them their own.

start.title: Getting started
start.summary: Register the library, point it at your settings routes and put the board on a page.

1.title: One registration
1.text: `AddOSBlazorSettings` also registers `OS.Blazor`, so you do not call both.

2.title: Three routes
2.text: The page talks to a list route, a section route and a save route under one `Root`.

3.title: Texts order
3.text: The library texts must be added before the locale is built.

4.title: Server not included
4.text: This package is only the browser side; your server serves the routes.

1.title: Registering
1.text:
`AddOSBlazorSettings` registers `SettingClient`, `SettingText` and the options. It also calls `AddOSBlazor` for you when that is not done yet, and adds the package's own English and Persian texts at the same time.

Calling it a second time changes nothing, so a shared setup method may call it safely.

2.title: The routes
2.text:
`SettingClient` calls three routes under `Root` (default `settings`): `GET {Root}/sections` lists the sections, `GET {Root}/sections/{code}` reads one, and `POST {Root}/sections/{code}` saves it. Scope goes in the query as `kind` and `id`.

The replies must be the standard `OSResult` shape that `ApiClient` reads. Your server side is not part of this package.

3.title: Texts order
3.text:
The locale copies its text sources when `AddOSBlazor` runs. If your app calls `AddOSBlazor` first, `AddOSBlazorSettings` can no longer add its texts, and the page shows raw keys such as `settings.board.find`.

In that case add them yourself inside `AddOSBlazor`, as the last sample shows.

4.title: Section and item texts
4.text: Titles of sections and settings come from your own locale files, not from this package: `settings.sections.{code}.title` style keys of your choice (the section sends its own `TitleKey`), and `settings.items.{key}.title` for each setting. See the texts topic.

own-route.title: Use another route
own-route.note: `Root` is trimmed of slashes, and an empty value is refused.

texts-after-blazor.title: Add the texts yourself
texts-after-blazor.note: Needed only when `AddOSBlazor` already ran with its own options.

routes.title: The calls it makes
routes.note: The three routes with their scope, as the client sends them.

type.SettingsUiEx: `AddOSBlazorSettings`: registers the client, the texts service and the options.
type.SettingsUiOptions: The only option is `Root`, the route prefix of the server.
type.SettingClient: Three calls over `ApiClient`: sections, one section, save.

SettingsUiOptions.Root: The route prefix, without leading or trailing slash. Default `settings`.

SettingClient.IsConflict: True when a failed save carries the code `settings.errors.conflict`.

board.title: The board
board.summary: The admin page and its parts: section list, section sheet, scopes, search, add and reset.

2.title: Scopes
2.text: Give it `Scopes` to let the administrator edit per shop, per tenant or any other scope.

3.title: Preview
3.text: A `Preview` template shows your own live preview next to the form.

4.title: Part components
4.text: The row, sheet, field, add and reset parts are public and can be reused alone.

1.title: The page
1.text:
The board loads the section list and then each section. A row shows the section title, how many values were changed and warnings such as an invalid stored value or a missing key. From a row you can view, edit or reset the section.

A search box finds sections by title and also by the titles and keys of the settings inside them.

2.title: Scopes
2.text:
Without `Scopes` the board edits the whole-app values. With `SettingScopeOption` items (a `Kind`, an `Id` and a `Name`) it shows a scope picker. A scope's value starts as the whole-app value; the administrator can give it its own value and later send it back.

Some settings cannot differ per scope. They stay locked in the scope view with a note.

3.title: The section sheet
3.text:
Editing happens in `OSSettingSheet`, a dialog. It has a View and an Edit mode, a counter of unsaved changes, and asks before closing with unsaved work.

When the server answers a save with a field error, the message appears under that setting; a general error shows at the top.

4.title: Preview and parts
4.text:
`Preview` is a `RenderFragment<SettingDesk>`: your markup receives the live editing state, so it can show, for example, how an e-mail would look before you save.

`OSSettingRow`, `OSSettingField`, `OSSettingAdd` and `OSSettingReset` are the parts the board is built from. They need the same services as the board; use them only if you build a custom layout.

scopes.title: With scopes
scopes.note: Each option has a scope kind and an id; the names are shown as given.

preview.title: A live preview
preview.note: The template gets the current editing state.

type.OSSettingSheet: The dialog that views or edits one section.
type.OSSettingRow: One line in the list, with chips and the view, edit and reset buttons.
type.OSSettingField: One setting: the right editor for its kind, its state chips and its error.
type.OSSettingAdd: Asks for a scope and a section before opening the editor.
type.OSSettingReset: Confirms and sends the reset of a section's own values.
type.SettingScopeOption: A scope the administrator can pick: kind, id and display name.

SettingScopeOption.Kind: The scope kind; 0 is reserved for the whole app.
SettingScopeOption.Id: The scope id inside its kind.
SettingScopeOption.Name: The name shown in the picker.

editing.title: Editing state
editing.summary: `SettingDesk` holds the drafts of one section: what changed, what is wrong, what was reset and what clashed with someone else.

1.title: No Razor
1.text: `SettingDesk` is plain C#, so you can test or reuse it without a browser.

2.title: Drafts
2.text: A value equal to the saved one is not a change.

3.title: Reset
3.text: Reset goes back to the default at app level and back to the app value in a scope.

4.title: Conflicts
4.text: After a refused save, `Rebase` keeps your drafts and marks what the other person changed.

1.title: Drafts and changes
1.text:
`Set` records what the user typed. Typing the saved value again removes the draft, so `DirtyCount` counts only real changes. `ToSave` builds the `SettingSaveModel` with only those changes, with numbers written in Latin digits.

`Undo` drops one draft and `Clear` drops all.

2.title: Checks
2.text: `FaultOf` returns the error key of the first problem (see the checking topic) and `FaultCount` counts them. The page keeps the Save button off while any fault remains.

3.title: Resets and scopes
3.text:
`Reset` marks a setting to go back. In the app view it shows the default; in a scope view `Value` returns `null`, meaning the scope follows the app again. `Own` gives a scope its own value, starting from the current one.

A setting that can only change at app level is `IsOutOfScope` in a scope view.

4.title: Secrets and conflicts
4.text:
A secret's value never reaches the browser. An empty secret draft is not a change; a filled one is. `HasSecret` on the item tells whether a value exists.

When a save is refused as a conflict, the page loads the fresh section and calls `Rebase`. Your drafts stay, and `ConflictOf` returns what the other person saved so you can keep yours (`KeepMine`) or take theirs (`Undo`).

draft.title: Make a change
draft.note: Setting the saved value again would not count.

fault.title: A wrong value
fault.note: The desk gives the error key, the field turns it into a message.

reset.title: Reset in the app and in a scope
reset.note: A scope returns `null` and so follows the app.

conflict.title: Someone saved first
conflict.note: Your draft stays and their value is kept beside it.

type.SettingDesk: The editing state of one section.

SettingDesk.Set: Records a typed value; a value equal to the saved one clears the draft.
SettingDesk.ToSave: Builds the save request with only the changed settings.
SettingDesk.Reset: Marks the setting to go back to its default (app) or to the app value (scope).
SettingDesk.Own: Gives a scope its own value, starting from the current one.
SettingDesk.Rebase: Takes a fresh section after a conflict and marks the settings that changed underneath you.
SettingDesk.FaultOf: The error key of the draft, or `null` when it is valid.
SettingDesk.Value: What the field shows now: the draft, the saved value, or `null` after a scope reset.

checking.title: Checking values
checking.summary: The browser checks a value with the same kinds the server uses, and accepts Persian and Arabic digits for numbers.

1.title: Same rules
1.text: `SettingCheck` calls the kinds of `OS.Settings.Abstractions`, so the browser and the server cannot drift apart.

2.title: Error keys
2.text: A failure returns a key such as `settings.errors.range`, which the page turns into a message.

3.title: Digits
3.text: Numbers and durations accept Persian and Arabic digits and the Arabic decimal mark.

4.title: Server is the gate
4.text: The browser check only saves a round trip; the server checks again.

1.title: What it checks
1.text:
`Check` takes a setting and a typed text and returns `null` for valid or an error key. The kinds are text, integer, decimal, boolean, url, path, duration, choice and list. Their limits (range, maximum length, allowed options) come from the setting's `Rules`.

A secret only has to be non-empty.

2.title: Digits
2.text: Before checking an integer, a decimal or a duration, `Latin` turns `۱۲٫۵` into `12.5`. The same step runs when the value is saved, so the server always receives Latin digits. Text, url and choice values are not changed.

3.title: Durations and lists
3.text:
A duration is written as `hh:mm:ss`, with days as `d.hh:mm:ss`; a bare number is refused because it would mean days. The page shows an amount and a unit and converts them with `Duration` and `TryDuration`.

Lists are comma separated; `Split` and `Join` convert them.

persian-digits.title: Persian digits
persian-digits.note: Accepted for numbers, left alone in text.

durations.title: Durations
durations.note: A bare number is not a duration.

type.SettingCheck: Static helpers for checking, digits, durations and lists.

SettingCheck.Check: The error key for a typed value, or `null` when it is valid.
SettingCheck.Latin: Persian and Arabic digits and the Arabic decimal mark to Latin; trims the text.
SettingCheck.Duration: Seconds to the `hh:mm:ss` text the duration kind expects.
SettingCheck.TryDuration: Reads that text back; refuses negative values.

texts.title: Texts and formatting
texts.summary: Which locale keys the page reads, how values are shown, and how to write the texts of your own settings.

1.title: Package texts
1.text: Labels of the page and the error messages ship in English and Persian.

2.title: Your texts
2.text: Titles, hints, units and option names of your settings come from your locale files.

3.title: Fallback
3.text: A setting without a title shows its key; a missing hint or unit is simply left out.

4.title: Culture
4.text: Numbers and durations are shown in the current culture, digits included.

1.title: Keys of your settings
1.text:
For a setting with the key `mail.port` the page looks for `settings.items.mail.port.title`, `.hint` and `.unit`. A choice or list option is read from `settings.items.mail.port.options.{option}`.

Section titles and descriptions use the `TitleKey` and `DescriptionKey` your server sends. When a scope kind is listed, its name is `settings.board.scope-kinds.{kind}`.

2.title: Package keys
2.text: Everything else (`settings.board.*` for the page, `settings.errors.*` for messages) ships inside the package in `en-US` and `fa-IR`. You can override any key by adding your own text source after the package's.

3.title: Showing values
3.text:
`SettingText.Format` writes a value the way the page shows it: a boolean as On or Off, a duration in its best unit, an amount with its unit, a secret as dots, a list as its option names. `Bytes` writes a size.

`SettingsUiCodes` holds the key names, so you can read them in code instead of retyping them.

values.title: How values are shown
values.note: These run in English; Persian digits appear with a Persian culture.

own-keys.title: Add your own texts
own-keys.note: Your assembly is added after the package, so its keys win.

type.SettingText: Reads titles, hints, units and option names, and formats values for display.
type.SettingsUiCodes: The locale keys, icon names and limits the page uses.

SettingText.Format: A value as the page shows it.
SettingText.Title: The setting's title, or its key when no text exists.
SettingText.Bytes: A size in KB or MB.

styling.title: Styling
styling.summary: One CSS file, built on the OS.Blazor tokens, that follows light and dark themes and right-to-left layout.

2.title: Tokens
2.text: It reads the `OS.Blazor` color and size tokens, with its own `--os-set-*` names on top.

3.title: RTL
3.text: It uses logical properties, so Persian pages mirror by themselves.

1.title: Adding the file
1.text: Add `<link rel="stylesheet" href="_content/OS.Blazor.Settings/os-settings.css" />` next to the OS.Blazor styles, in `index.html` or `App.razor`.

2.title: Changing the look
2.text:
The board reads `--os-set-accent`, `--os-set-gap`, `--os-set-bg` and a few more, each falling back to an OS.Blazor token. Set them on `.os-set-board` or any parent to restyle only this page.

Colors follow the active theme, so no extra dark mode work is needed.

tokens.title: Change the accent
tokens.note: Only the board changes; other pages keep their colors.
